cues: My great-grandfather's name was Keh Yazh
They called him Sore Foot He lived on Big Mountain in the late 1800s
And he is the reason the stone breath exists
That's not his real name
That is the name I made up for my writings
I want to also respect the family
As his offspring is pretty much most of Big Mountain
Every morning he ran east towards the sunrise
Then he went to work A large flock of sheep and cornfields
That needed him every single day He also had horses
He was a singer He had many responsibilities
He ran with a small smooth river stone in his hand
About the size of a bird's egg As he ran
He would imagine that stone Resting on his tongue and his lips
He would relax his jaw He would relax his temples His eyes
His shoulders His back He would make sure that he was level
And not bouncing up and down Really easily controlling his breathing
Just balancing that small stone on his tongue
The picturing alone brings the water back to the dry mouth
So the thirst does not own you
It keeps the breath even and slow The heart rate low
The nervous system settle
On the hills he leaned from his ankles Not his waist
So his chest stayed open And he could breathe
When he got tired He softened his eyes
And took in the whole horizon Instead of staring at just one spot
Then word came of a twenty mile race against
Other tribes A gathering of Hopi, Zuni, Apache
And men and women from the plains
Who had traveled for weeks to be there
Imposing figures Languages he did not speak
Traditions he had never seen Only heard about
His family rode with him four days
Back then Everything was on foot or horseback
Later Wagons
And the prayers before it Were for clean lungs
Strong legs A fair mind
That would not react to provocation
He meditated He visioned
He did the sauna
The traditional sauna ceremony This is where the stone breath was The ultimate tool
Part of the whole preparation Of course he did not go to fight He went to run
And he finished strong Many times he won these races
And that's where his legend comes from
Here is why it works
Under stress And panic
We fall into tunnel vision
Our eyes narrow Onto the problem We hunch over We stop breathing well And we stop noticing What is around us
Each one makes the others worse Standing tall Widening your view And softening Your jaw Tells your body It is safe to think again
This practice came down from my family Hand to hand
Now it comes to you In our way
I was taught to share To ensure that The neighbor
The family member
The family across the way
Also has the tools To survive To grow
And to raise their children So this week Before a hard meeting Or a hard conversation
Hold something small in your hand Or simply imagine a pebble
Imagine its journey This stone is older than you
And it will be older than your grandchildren
Someday Imagine its texture
Give thanks that it is here with you today Stand tall
Look at the whole room Not just a problem
Then breathe in four Hold four
Breathe out For six
Nice and slow Hold for four
Do that again In for four
Hold for four Out For six
Hold For four
Do that Three more times
In for four Hold For four
Out For six Hold For four The last one
I'm going to do with you One Two Three Four Out For six
Hold For four
And For four
Now relax Sell it yourself
Notice how you feel Now Go and
Address that challenge Do the work.
